learning: No race data exists yet. Items to check after the first race: whether kp = 4 causes oscillation (steering_oscillation), whether base_speed 1.6 finishes within 3 s, and whether line_loss_events occur on the sharpest bends.
notes: Baseline geometry from the Builder, unchanged, with a proportional controller whose sensor weights scale with sensor x. last_direction line-loss recovery. Expected first result is an oval completion attempt; no measured results yet.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or earlier Integrator feedback. I kept the Geometry Builder's baseline geometry unchanged so the first race tests the proposal as written. The five sensors are at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 (positive = left). I set the sensor weights to x/0.03, giving -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1. A tape under the right-hand sensors then gives a negative signal, which steers right, and the signal stays within ±1. With |signal| ≤ 1, kp = 4 gives turn up to ±4, or about ±1400 PWM per wheel, which is enough authority for the bends without saturating. The integral gain is small (ki = 0.05) to avoid windup on the long bends. kd = 0.3 damps the response at the sensor lead distance of 0.05 m ahead of the axle. base_speed = 1.6 gives about 3685 PWM, which should be enough to average the roughly 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3 s, while leaving some margin for the slalom. Line loss uses 'last_direction' so the robot searches toward the side it last saw the line. The observation request keeps the Builder's requested measurements and adds controller_errors so exceptions are visible. Expected result: first completion attempt on the oval, with line-loss events and rms error as the main unknowns.
